about: Doctrine rules as DATA. Every implementation (Swift core, bb reference scorecard, any future page/app) reads this file; none hardcodes a pattern. `rules` is the CATALOG: each rule once, with its source text and every sensor that measures or enforces it. A rule with no sensor is folklore and is refused at load.

rules.source: CLAUDE.md first principle (specification before code); APPEND_SYSTEM.md 'Specification and action': a `Done when:` line before the first write/edit
APPEND_SYSTEM.md 'Custody and verification': end with `Verified:` naming the level actually reached; WISDOM.md rule 1
WISDOM.md rule 1 / CLAUDE.md 'Verify from outside': never round `ran` up to `deployed`; a `tested` claim needs a run after the last change
AGENTS.md 'Tool discipline': use edit for existing files; never overwrite something you have not read (the lens approximates: an edit must target a path already read, written or edited)
AGENTS.md 'Tool discipline': every long or network command gets a timeout
AGENTS.md 'Model and provider discipline': verify a free model responds, keep a fallback chain
CLAUDE.md language preferences; APPEND_SYSTEM.md: do not write Python or Node
CLAUDE.md / APPEND_SYSTEM.md: Nix or source, no Homebrew
CLAUDE.md conventions: API keys in the home directory are intentional, do not flag them
CLAUDE.md 'On the shell and the fleet': sample before rm / truncate / vacuum
CLAUDE.md 'On the shell and the fleet': write locally, scp, run; no nested quoting over ssh
CLAUDE.md 'Economy of tokens': read the slice you need (grep, offset/limit)
CLAUDE.md 'Resilience & Graceful Failure': exit codes and messages must make failure obvious
